name: Actissist
one_liner: A research smartphone app for early psychosis, based on CBT for psychosis, tested in UK trials. Not publicly available.
best_for: Clinicians and researchers interested in digital CBT for early psychosis
People taking part in a research study that offers Actissist
not_for: Anyone looking for an app to download today: it is not publicly available
Anyone in crisis: call or text 988
People who need treatment for psychosis: contact an early intervention service or psychiatrist
short_description: Actissist is a CBT-informed app for early psychosis from the University of Manchester, used only in research trials so far.
long_description: Actissist was developed by researchers at the University of Manchester as a smartphone app delivering CBT-informed support for people in early psychosis, with modules on voices, paranoia, perceived criticism, cannabis use and social withdrawal. It has been tested in two UK randomized trials: a 2018 proof-of-concept trial (36 people) that reported promising effects, and a larger 2024 trial (172 people) in which both Actissist and a symptom-monitoring control app improved, with no significant difference between them. We found no app-store listing or public release, so people cannot get it outside a study.
patient_summary: Actissist is a research app for people with early psychosis, based on CBT for psychosis. It has only been offered inside UK research studies, and you can't download it. If you're looking for help with psychosis, an early intervention service or psychiatrist is the place to start.

pricing.notes: Only offered to people taking part in research studies.

privacy.notes: Research app; data handling is set by each study's ethics approval. No public privacy policy found.

seo.title: Actissist: App for Schizophrenia & Psychosis | HeyPsych
seo.meta_description: Actissist helps people with schizophrenia and psychosis track symptoms, identify warning signs, and access coping strategies alongside treatment.

faqs.a: Actissist is designed for people with schizophrenia, schizoaffective disorder, or other psychotic disorders who are engaged in treatment. It's meant to support - not replace - professional care.

Actissist helps you track early warning signs and access coping strategies, which may help you respond earlier to emerging symptoms. It works best as part of a comprehensive treatment plan with your mental health team.

faqs.q: Is there evidence that Actissist works?
faqs.a: Actissist was developed based on clinical research into digital interventions for psychosis. While individual results vary, it's designed using evidence-based principles from CBT for psychosis.

faqs.q: Should I use Actissist without a treatment team?
faqs.a: Actissist is designed as a supplement to professional treatment, not a standalone tool. If you're experiencing psychosis, please connect with a mental health provider first.
